versions.changelog:
- Expanded file permissions: now documents reading and writing of .env and config.json files, plus library.json output on every library command.
- File permissions are clarified, including the default behavior and override options for config, token, and exercise catalog files.
- skill-card.md file removed.
- Minor metadata and documentation updates for accuracy and clarity.

### Version 1.0.6 of the Speediance skill introduces a new agent-friendly session summary command.

- Added `today` command to retrieve all workout sessions for the current (or a specified) day in a normalized, type-agnostic format.
- Improved session detail output: `session <id>` now identifies the session type (`kind: program | free | ""`) and emits unmodified API data per type.
- Updated help/docs to recommend `today` as the easiest way to fetch recent activity without worrying about session types (program, free lift, or cardio).
- Unified and clarified data fields, providing a consistent shape for automated consumers.
- Minor documentation and structural updates; `skill-card.md` removed.

Speediance v1.0.5

- Token and config file locations are now OS-aware: by default, session tokens are cached in your OS user-cache directory, and config.json can reside in the working directory or OS user-config dir.
- Legacy token cache (.token.json) in the working directory is now auto-migrated to the new cache location.
- New environment variables: SPEEDIANCE_CONFIG to override the config file path, and SPEEDIANCE_TOKEN_CACHE to override the token cache location.
- Documentation updated for clarity on configuration, token location, and migration behavior.
- Improved tests and internal logic for config and token file discovery, migration, and usage.
- No breaking changes to core commands or output.

- Added support for parsing a .env file to load SPEEDIANCE_* environment variables automatically, ensuring only relevant keys are read and injected.
- Security improvement: The .env parser ignores unrelated variables, preventing accidental environment injection from unrelated keys.
- Documentation updates to clarify new .env handling and to note that only SPEEDIANCE_* keys are considered.
- Added new CLAUDE.md documentation; removed legacy skill-card.md file.
- Minor internal code and test updates related to configuration handling.

- Removed Markdown week-sheet sync: CLI no longer writes sessions into local Markdown files.
- Clarified that the CLI only reads and emits structured workout data; storage is up to the user.
- Cleaned up permissions and documentation references to reflect feature removals.
- Added RELEASING.md; removed obsolete internal/sheet and sync-related files.
- Documentation and metadata updated for greater clarity and accuracy.

Major update: Migrates from a Python module to a static Go binary, modernizing install and usage.

- Replaces Python codebase with a single static Go binary (no Python or other runtime needed).
- New `speediance-cli` includes all previous functionality via a command-based interface.
- Updated install instructions (download binary or `go install`; Python commands removed).
- Adds support for `.env` credential files and enhanced config management commands.
- Removes Python dependencies, source files, and related documentation.

- Expanded skill description to clarify all features and detail required file/network permissions.
- Added explicit permissions section listing file read/write and network access in SKILL.md metadata.
- Description now documents automatic session token caching and optional Markdown week-sheet sync.
- Minor wording, clarification, and formatting improvements across documentation.

Initial release of the Speediance skill.

- Read completed workouts and per-set session details from your Speediance (Gym Monster) device via its cloud API.
- Browse and search the full exercise catalog; output as JSON or save snapshots for offline use.
- Push author-custom training programs directly to your device, ready to run.
- Environment variable and config file support for credentials and device configuration.
- Optional sync of completed sessions into Markdown workout checklists.
- Unofficial tool, reverse-engineered for personal use; tested on Gym Monster v1.
